The strongest matches I found are quick edamame snacks. They’re savory, vegan, and rich in plant protein; times assume the frozen edamame is microwave-ready.

- **Soy-sesame chili edamame — about 3–5 minutes, ~15 g protein per serving.** Microwave 1 cup shelled edamame for 2–3 minutes, drain, and toss with 1 tsp soy sauce or tamari, ½ tsp sesame oil, and chili flakes. A search result attributed the nutrition estimate to Nutritiously Delicia. [Search results](https://www.google.com/search?q=5+minute+vegan+snack+edamame+protein+recipe+nutrition)
- **Simple seasoned edamame — about 3–5 minutes, ~12 g protein per serving.** Warm shelled edamame and season to taste with salt, chili, or lemon. Dietetic Directions lists about 120 calories, 12 g protein, and 8 g fiber for its 5-minute recipe. [Dietetic Directions](https://dieteticdirections.com/)
- **Edamame crunch salad — about 5 minutes, ~17 g protein per cup of edamame.** Toss edamame with shredded carrot and cabbage; add sesame seeds and a light soy or citrus dressing. The protein figure is for the edamame itself, so the finished serving depends on how much you use. [Confessions of a Mother Runner](https://confessionsofamotherrunner.com/)

The protein and timing figures are source-reported estimates and may vary by portion and brand. `FINAL ANSWER: Try soy-sesame chili edamame for the clearest match: about 3–5 minutes and 15 g protein per serving.`
